boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Mount Zion Church record (December 28, 1861) in Operations in Northeast Missouri [December 1861]. The December 27 skirmish near Hallsville and Prentiss's march from Palmyra are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives detachments of the 3rd Missouri Cavalry (about 240) and Birge's Sharpshooters (about 200), 440 in the forces table, and an unknown Confederate force; the frozen description says 5 mounted companies and 2 companies of sharpshooters. Prentiss says five troops of cavalry and five companies of sharpshooters numbering 470 marched, and that prisoners put the enemy near 900. Britton gives the same 470 and nine hundred.
claims.rationale: Prentiss's marching force and his prisoners' estimate; the company counts in the frozen description and the report differ. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Caleb Dorsey (read 'Horsey' in OCR) and Brigadier General Benjamin M. Prentiss. Prentiss directed the attack; he says Glover moved at the double-quick to support the three engaged companies and the two reserve companies came in as the enemy gave way.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report; no Confederate account was inspected and there is no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 282 (US 72; CS 210). Prentiss reports 3 killed, 17 severely and 46 slightly wounded for Mount Zion and the previous evening's skirmish together, and enemy losses of 25 killed and 150 wounded, with 30 prisoners taken; Britton repeats these figures.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Prentiss's Union figures include the December 27 skirmish near Hallsville and must not be assigned to this record alone.

open_questions: The live NPS page for MO010 is an empty template; the frozen CWSAC row is that family's evidence. Dorsey's side, returns and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Prentiss's January 4, 1862 report is an interested Union account, the same author family as the registered Prentiss Shiloh selections (group or-prentiss). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, vol. I (second edition, 1891) is a retrospective history by a Union soldier of the border army, based by its title page on the official reports; it is not independent of the report families. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
